terms.grammar: the present subjunctive, first person plural, in -āmus (-ēmus in the first conjugation); negative nē
evidence: Ter. Eun. 459: Eāmus ergō ad cēnam
Hor. S. 1.1.27: āmōtō quaerāmus sēria lūdō
terms.comment: Often after age or agite, “come on”. Negative nē: nē exspectēmus quidem, dum rogēmur, let’s not even wait to be asked.

phrases.latin: Eāmus ergō ad cēnam: quid stās?
phrases.english: Let’s go to dinner, then: why are you standing there?
Let’s go; lead the way, please.

phrases.latin: sed tamen āmōtō quaerāmus sēria lūdō
phrases.english: but still, joking aside, let’s turn to serious things

phrases.latin: ergō vīvāmus, dum licet esse bene
phrases.english: so let’s live, while we may have a good time

phrases.latin: nē exspectēmus quidem, dum rogēmur; studium semper adsit, cūnctātiō absit
phrases.english: let’s not even wait to be asked; let eagerness always be there and hesitation never

phrases.latin: cantantēs licet ūsque (minus via laedit) eāmus
phrases.english: let’s go singing all the way (the road hurts less)

phrases.latin: sed cum dīcitur, 'eāmus, faciāmus,' et pudet nōn esse impudentem
phrases.english: but when someone says “let’s go, let’s do it”, one is ashamed not to be shameless

sources: Lewis & Short: eo
